bibl.title: The Russia-Ukraine Conflict: Its Implications for the Global Food Supply Chains

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the global food supply chain under the Russia-Ukraine war, across six impact areas that a panel of experts selected before the literature was searched
span.quote: This paper aims to analyze the impacts of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine on the effectiveness and responsiveness of the global food supply chains.

span.label: what strategies or solutions may be implemented to mitigate the conflict's impacts on global food supply chains
span.quote: The related research question is as follows. What strategies or solutions may be implemented to mitigate the impacts of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine on global food supply chains?

span.label: a PRISMA review of grey and peer-reviewed literature across six expert-selected impact areas, with mitigation strategies for each
span.quote: Six key areas of the food supply chain that would be impacted due to the ongoing war were highlighted: (a) Food production, processing, and storage, (b) Food transport logistics, (c) Food market/retail, (d) Consumers, (e) Food dependent services, and (f) Food quality.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The hypothesis underlying this research has been confirmed in that there will be significant impacts on the effectiveness and responsiveness of global food supply chains as a result of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine.

span.label: a supply shock propagating from two exporting countries into food prices, availability, quality and fraud worldwide, on top of an unfinished COVID-19 disruption
span.quote: Since the war began, wheat prices have risen over forty percent, to prices not seen since the 2007–2008 World Food Price Crisis

span.label: a two-round e-Delphi with 13 participants to identify and rank the impacts, the top six becoming the review's scope; then a PRISMA search of grey literature and databases, one impact area per co-author
span.term: a two-round e-Delphi with 13 participants to identify and rank the impacts, the top six becoming the review's scope; then a PRISMA search of grey literature and databases, one impact area per co-author
span.quote: The impact categories that are the focus of this research were initially identified with expert consultation using a qualitative two-round e-Delphi method \ [11, 12\] with 13 participants. The first round was used to identify potential impacts of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on food supply chains based on the hypothesis that significant impacts on the effectiveness and responsiveness of global food supply chains are the result of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. The second round asked participants to rank the impacts identified in the first round. The top six impacts defined the impact areas followed up in the review synthesis.

span.label: why the agricultural collapse is self-reinforcing: about 70% of Ukraine's petrol and diesel came from Russia and Belarus, so the same conflict that closes the market also removes the fuel needed to plant, harvest and move what is left
span.quote: the Ukrainian agri-production industry depends heavily on fuel imports, with about 70% of imports of petrol and diesel coming from the Russian Federation and Belarus

span.label: why poultry and cattle recover on different clocks - a broiler is 21 days as an egg and 42 out of it, so flocks return within months of a maize harvest, while cattle take three or four years
span.term: biological recovery time as an economic constraint
span.quote: The expected 2022 mass slaughter of beef cattle will impact Ukrainian cattle farming for years. Cattle farming would likely not recover until three or four years after access to consistent animal feed was reestablished.

span.label: why some shortfalls hurt and others do not: edible oils substitute for one another and store well, so removing the world's largest sunflower oil exporter is mostly a financial event; pharmaceuticals do not substitute, because labelling, dosage and formulary differ across borders
span.quote: Edible fats remain extremely fungible, with other oils substituting for a sunflower oil well. Oils can also be stored for long periods of time, and major blocs such as the EU and the United States maintain significant reserves.

span.label: the route from supply shock to food safety: shortage plus price spike plus substitution pressure creates the conditions for adulteration, and the paper names the four Ukrainian products most exposed - honey, sunflower oil, grains and seafood
span.term: scarcity as an opening for fraud
span.quote: Similarly, the Russian invasion of Ukraine could increase the opportunities for food fraud and may impact global food traceability systems.

span.label: the paper's conclusion from its own historical cases: absent large external investment of the kind that followed the Second World War, the economic damage outlasts the conflict by generations
span.quote: Without strong external intervention to rebuild, Ukraine will likely remain impoverished by this conflict for generations to come.

span.label: THE PAPER GIVES UKRAINE'S CEREAL EXPORT RANK AS SECOND IN ONE SECTION AND FOURTH IN ANOTHER, both flatly and with different citations - a self-inconsistency in a headline figure, not a hedge
span.quote: Before the invasion, Ukraine was the fourth largest exporter of cereals in the world and one of the world’s largest producers, harvesting over 3.7% of the world’s total cereals

span.label: and the same divergence at smaller scale on wheat: 3.2% versus 3.3% of global production, 9.1% versus 9% of exports
span.note: about this quote: 2026-08-25 terminal-a. FLATTENED EXPONENT IN THIS QUOTE - THE NUMBER IS WRONG BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE AS IT STANDS. The staged text reads '18.06 × 106', where the paper writes 10 to the power 6. The superscript was pushed onto the line by the PDF extractor. The quote is verbatim to the staged text and its anchor is sound; the STAGED TEXT is what is damaged. NOT repaired - repair means re-staging the body and re-anchoring the record. Found by CLAUDE_B, row chk_flattened_exponent_in_a_quote.
span.quote: Most important to the global food system is where this wheat and small grain production is exported, Ukraine is the 5th ranked global exporter of wheat at 18.06 × 106 tonnes in 2020 which is 9% of global wheat exports (FAOStat).

span.label: the mechanism is in the methods and is not presented as a limitation: each impact area was searched by one co-author in their own area of expertise, corroborated by the others - a division of labour with no stated step for reconciling figures BETWEEN areas
span.quote: Each impact area was searched in this way by one of the co-authors based on their area of expertise, supported and corroborated by the other co-authors.

span.label: the scope is what thirteen experts ranked in the top six; sustainability was proposed and excluded, so an impact absent from this paper may have been considered and voted out rather than not existing
span.quote: The participants in the e-Delphi identified the top six supply chain impacts of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as shown in Figure 1. Additional impacts that were not part of the top six impacts included impacts on sustainability.

span.label: searches ran only from 13 March to 14 May 2022 - weeks into a war whose effects the paper repeatedly projects years forward
span.quote: A grey literature search plan was developed incorporating three different searching strategies: (1) customized Google search, (2) targeted websites, and (3) news reports. The grey literature search was supplemented with relevant peer-reviewed articles from the SCOPUS and Google Scholar databases using the same search terms: “Ukrain\*”, “Russi\*”, “war”, and the keywords of each of the identified impact areas. Each impact area was searched in this way by one of the co-authors based on their area of expertise, supported and corroborated by the other co-authors. Searches were performed from 13 March 2022 to 14 May 2022.

span.label: much of the evidence is grey literature by design, which the authors defend as necessary for a timely and evolving topic rather than treat as a weakness
span.quote: Large-scale review syntheses, especially those concerning timely and evolving topics, have grey literature as an important source of information

span.label: food quality and safety had very little academic research behind them at the time of writing, so that section rests on analogy to Syria, Yemen and Chernobyl rather than on studies of this conflict
span.quote: Although studies have focused on the effect of the invasion of Ukraine by Russia on the food supply chain from an economic point of view \ [79\], very little academic research has been done on the impact of this crisis on food quality and safety.

span.label: selecting the six impact areas by a two-round e-Delphi of 13 experts BEFORE the literature search, and reporting which candidate impacts did not make the top six
span.note: eliminates: the review's scope being set by what the authors happened to find - the selection is prior, structured, and its losers are named. It does NOT eliminate the panel being wrong about what would matter · outcome: partial
span.quote: The impact categories that are the focus of this research were initially identified with expert consultation using a qualitative two-round e-Delphi method \ [11, 12\] with 13 participants. The first round was used to identify potential impacts of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on food supply chains based on the hypothesis that significant impacts on the effectiveness and responsiveness of global food supply chains are the result of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. The second round asked participants to rank the impacts identified in the first round. The top six impacts defined the impact areas followed up in the review synthesis.

span.label: a PRISMA-reported search with a written grey literature plan naming resources, terms, websites, limits and dates
span.note: eliminates: an unreproducible search - the strategy, the databases and the exact window are all stated · outcome: held
span.quote: Elements to be reported according to a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) include a description of all information sources in the search, the name of the person conducting the search, the date the search was performed, and a full search strategy of at least one database including all search terms and combinations

span.label: assigning each impact area to the co-author with expertise in it, with corroboration by the others
span.note: eliminates: one reviewer covering six specialist domains badly - AND IT IS ALSO THE CAUSE OF THE SECOND-VERSUS-FOURTH CONTRADICTION. The corroboration step operated within areas and evidently not across them · outcome: partial
span.quote: Each impact area was searched in this way by one of the co-authors based on their area of expertise, supported and corroborated by the other co-authors.

span.label: a satellite Vegetation Condition Index comparison of March 2021 against March 2022, normalised against the historical NDVI range for the same period
span.note: eliminates: a claimed reduction in planting resting on reports from a war zone - the index is normalised to the same calendar window in a prior year, so seasonality is differenced out · outcome: held
span.quote: The VCI evaluates the current vegetation health compared to the historical trends using the current dekadal Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to its long-term minimum and maximum, so that the data is normalized by the historical range of NDVI values for the same time period.

span.label: stating explicitly where the impact will be SMALL - sunflower oil attenuated by fungibility, maize replaceable from three US states, poultry prices barely moved, pharmaceutical shortages minor against a $1.2 trillion market
span.note: eliminates: a catastrophe framing applied uniformly - the paper distinguishes what the world loses from what Ukraine loses, and says so in the sections where the answer is inconvenient to its own headline · outcome: held
span.quote: Despite the fact that the war threatens to remove billions of dollars and trillions of calories from the global marketplace through the disruption of Ukrainian seed oil shipments, the impact on the consumer is likely to be attenuated.

span.label: using prior shocks with known outcomes as calibration - the 2007-08 food price crisis, Syria's 90% export collapse, Transnistria and South Ossetia's halved GDP, Bangladesh's 45-year recovery
span.note: eliminates: forecasts with no reference class; each projection is anchored to a case where the outcome is already known · outcome: held
span.quote: Syria’s gross exports amounted to $11.9 billion the year before the war, and most recently were measured at $0.6 billion \ [46\]: a real and sustained reduction of over 90% of the country’s exports in the wake of the Russian bombing, which is a plausible outcome for Ukraine as well.

span.label: noting that other recent wars - Tigray, Nagorno-Karabakh - were functionally invisible in global markets
span.note: eliminates: the assumption that any war disrupts global food supply; the claim is about THIS conflict's particular position in the trade network, and the counter-examples are named · outcome: held
span.quote: Other recent wars such as the Tigray War in Ethiopia or the Nagorno-Karabakh War in Azerbaijan have not been anticipated by market actors to be as disruptive to food and medical supply chains and have been functionally invisible when looking at global markets.

span.label: food supply chains
span.quote: This paper aims to analyze the impacts of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine on the effectiveness and responsiveness of the global food supply chains.

span.label: e-Delphi
span.quote: The participants in the e-Delphi identified the top six supply chain impacts of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as shown in Figure 1. Additional impacts that were not part of the top six impacts included impacts on sustainability.

span.label: grey literature
span.quote: Large-scale review syntheses, especially those concerning timely and evolving topics, have grey literature as an important source of information

span.label: food fraud
span.quote: The key characteristics of food fraud are non-compliance with food laws, and misleading the consumer for financial gain. Food fraud can include a substitution of species, adding or replacing food ingredients with undeclared substitutes, and discrepancies in food production or farming method

span.label: food access
span.quote: In the short term, the main food-security concern in Ukraine is food access, not food availability, since available stocks in Ukraine were approximately 1.14-fold greater than the estimated annual demand

span.label: food availability
span.quote: In the short term, the main food-security concern in Ukraine is food access, not food availability, since available stocks in Ukraine were approximately 1.14-fold greater than the estimated annual demand

span.label: sunflower oil
span.quote: The invasion of Ukraine provides a unique opportunity for fraudsters to replace sunflower oil with refined rapeseed oil, mineral oil, castor oil, cottonseed oil, among others

span.label: wheat
span.quote: Ukraine’s wheat production is 3.2% of global production and exports are 9.1% of the global wheat exports

span.label: fuel imports
span.quote: the Ukrainian agri-production industry depends heavily on fuel imports, with about 70% of imports of petrol and diesel coming from the Russian Federation and Belarus

span.label: VCI
span.quote: The VCI evaluates the current vegetation health compared to the historical trends using the current dekadal Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to its long-term minimum and maximum, so that the data is normalized by the historical range of NDVI values for the same time period.

span.label: wheat → food supply chains
span.note: TWO INCOMPATIBLE VALUES FOR ONE QUANTITY, INSIDE ONE PAPER. Ukraine is the SECOND largest cereal exporter in section 3.2.1 and the FOURTH largest in section 3.2.4, each stated flatly with its own citation. There is no relation type for `this record asserts X and also asserts not-X`, and no field on a content_tags row for `contradicted by another row in the same record`. The corpus can hold both numbers and cannot hold the fact that they disagree
span.quote: Ukraine exported more than $9.4bn worth of cereals in 2020, around one-fifth of its total exports, and it is ranked second global cereal exporter, whereas the US is first ranked

span.label: e-Delphi → food supply chains
span.note: A METHOD THAT DETERMINES WHAT THE PAPER IS ABOUT. The panel's ranking did not measure the world; it selected which six impacts would be researched, and sustainability lost. That is a relation between a PROCEDURE and the SCOPE OF A CLAIM - not between two concepts in the world - and none of the eight types reaches it. It is the same gap as tsao2017's `maturity -> Ga2O3`: our vocabulary describes the world and cannot describe an appraisal or a choice about the world
span.quote: The participants in the e-Delphi identified the top six supply chain impacts of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as shown in Figure 1. Additional impacts that were not part of the top six impacts included impacts on sustainability.

span.label: the six impact areas - CHOSEN BY VOTE BEFORE THE EVIDENCE WAS GATHERED. Thirteen experts proposed impacts in round one and ranked them in round two, and the TOP SIX became the paper's scope. Sustainability was named and did not make the cut. So the review's coverage is a measure of what a panel expected to matter in March 2022, not of what the literature contains
span.quote: The participants in the e-Delphi identified the top six supply chain impacts of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as shown in Figure 1. Additional impacts that were not part of the top six impacts included impacts on sustainability.

span.label: Ukraine's rank as a cereal exporter, IN THIS PAPER - SECOND IN SECTION 3.2.1 AND FOURTH IN SECTION 3.2.4. Both are stated flatly, 16,000 characters apart, with different citations. Neither is hedged and neither refers to the other. A reader quoting `this paper says Ukraine is the Nth largest cereal exporter` can be right twice with different N
span.quote: Ukraine exported more than $9.4bn worth of cereals in 2020, around one-fifth of its total exports, and it is ranked second global cereal exporter, whereas the US is first ranked

span.label: the same divergence at a smaller scale, on wheat: production is 3.2% of global in one section and 3.3% in another, exports 9.1% and then 9%. Individually these are rounding; TOGETHER WITH THE RANK THEY ARE A PATTERN, and the methods section names the mechanism - one co-author per impact area, each searching independently
span.quote: Ukraine’s wheat production is 3.2% of global production and exports are 9.1% of the global wheat exports

span.label: impact, as this paper uses it - A FORECAST FOR MOST OF THE SIX AREAS, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The searches ran 13 March to 14 May 2022, weeks into the war, so claims like the 2022 cattle slaughter, the 2023 meat shortfall and the recovery timescales are predictions stated in the present tense
span.quote: The expected 2022 mass slaughter of beef cattle will impact Ukrainian cattle farming for years. Cattle farming would likely not recover until three or four years after access to consistent animal feed was reestablished.

span.label: food security, in the Ukrainian short term - ACCESS, NOT AVAILABILITY, and the paper is careful to separate them: stocks inside Ukraine were about 1.14 times annual demand. The shortage is of transport, fuel and labour rather than of food, which is why the mitigation list is about logistics
span.quote: In the short term, the main food-security concern in Ukraine is food access, not food availability, since available stocks in Ukraine were approximately 1.14-fold greater than the estimated annual demand

span.label: builds-on → the 2007-2008 World Food Price Crisis, in which Ukraine's export tariffs removed over $300 million of wheat from world markets
span.note: and the comparison is used to argue the reference case UNDERSTATES the present one: the removal was a minor exacerbating factor then, and world dependence on Ukrainian cereals has grown since
span.quote: The removal of Ukrainian wheat from export markets was a minor exacerbating factor in the food price crisis, but in the years since the world has become more dependent on Ukrainian cereals.

span.label: confirms → FAO's recommended actions for alleviating the food security challenge, focused on resuming production and protecting farmers
span.quote: The quick solution to this crisis is to halt the war and allow agricultural production to resume immediately and safely to avoid further potential impacts on food security in Ukraine—and beyond—in the coming days, weeks, and months.

span.label: builds-on → Bentley's recommendation to expand wheat production in high-productivity regions and raise productivity where it is low
span.quote: recommends expanding wheat production in high-productivity areas (North America and Europe) and in regions with suitable conditions (Sudan and Nigeria are promising), and by increasing productivity in places where it is low (such as Ethiopia and Turkey).

span.label: critiques → the body of work analysing this invasion's food supply effects from an economic point of view, which has left food quality and safety almost unstudied
span.quote: Although studies have focused on the effect of the invasion of Ukraine by Russia on the food supply chain from an economic point of view \ [79\], very little academic research has been done on the impact of this crisis on food quality and safety.

span.label: food access —distinct-from→ food availability
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the distinction carries the paper's whole short-term diagnosis: stocks inside Ukraine were about 1.14x annual demand, so the shortage was of transport and labour
span.quote: In the short term, the main food-security concern in Ukraine is food access, not food availability, since available stocks in Ukraine were approximately 1.14-fold greater than the estimated annual demand

span.label: fuel imports —causes→ wheat
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — signed from a survey figure rather than an assertion - 20% of 1,300 businesses, and the direction is about planting rather than about the crop already in the ground
span.quote: FAO reports that only 20% of 1300 large agri-businesses surveyed by the Ukrainian Government have enough fuel for planting this spring

span.label: food fraud —causes→ sunflower oil
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.8 — the paper's verb is `provides a unique opportunity`, which is a forecast about incentives rather than an observed rise. Weight 0.8 for that
span.quote: Honey, sunflower oil, grains, and seafood are among the main foodstuffs produced in Ukraine and that are most vulnerable to food fraud.

span.label: VCI —operationalised-as→ wheat
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — the index measures vegetation health, which the paper reads as planting activity in the crop Oblasts. One inferential step past what VCI directly reports
span.quote: The central Oblasts are where Ukraine’s major agricultural crops are produced and it can be seen that these central regions have a 20–25% reduction in VCI currently suggesting growth and planting is significantly reduced.

span.label: six impact areas, selected by expert ranking rather than by the literature: production/processing/storage, transport logistics, market/retail, consumers, food-dependent services, food quality
span.quote: Six key areas of the food supply chain that would be impacted due to the ongoing war were highlighted: (a) Food production, processing, and storage, (b) Food transport logistics, (c) Food market/retail, (d) Consumers, (e) Food dependent services, and (f) Food quality.

span.label: the most affected economies are in Europe and Africa, with the advice to source from the Americas, Middle East, Australasia and less-affected parts of Asia and Africa
span.quote: Research showed that although this conflict will affect the majority of the economies, however, the most affected economies are in Europe and Africa.

span.label: the short-term Ukrainian problem is food ACCESS not availability - domestic stocks were about 1.14 times annual demand
span.quote: In the short term, the main food-security concern in Ukraine is food access, not food availability, since available stocks in Ukraine were approximately 1.14-fold greater than the estimated annual demand

span.label: where the world's loss is small and stated as such: sunflower oil is substitutable and storable, maize is replaceable from three US states, poultry prices barely move
span.quote: Despite the fact that the war threatens to remove billions of dollars and trillions of calories from the global marketplace through the disruption of Ukrainian seed oil shipments, the impact on the consumer is likely to be attenuated.

span.label: and where it is not: potable water for millions of Ukrainians has no local substitute, and the paper puts possible related deaths in the hundreds of thousands
span.quote: While water is not financially expensive, local sources sufficient to replace the water sources for tens of millions of Ukrainians simply do not exist. Deaths related to compromised water supplies could easily reach hundreds of thousands, despite the low cost of restoring stable water access once eventually achieved.

span.label: food quality and safety had almost no academic research behind them for this conflict at the time of writing
span.quote: Although studies have focused on the effect of the invasion of Ukraine by Russia on the food supply chain from an economic point of view \ [79\], very little academic research has been done on the impact of this crisis on food quality and safety.

span.label: food fraud = non-compliance with food laws and misleading the consumer for financial gain, including species substitution, undeclared substitutes and false production or farming claims
span.quote: The key characteristics of food fraud are non-compliance with food laws, and misleading the consumer for financial gain. Food fraud can include a substitution of species, adding or replacing food ingredients with undeclared substitutes, and discrepancies in food production or farming method

span.label: the Vegetation Condition Index compares current vegetation health to the historical NDVI range for the same period, separating weather from seasonal cover
span.quote: The VCI evaluates the current vegetation health compared to the historical trends using the current dekadal Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to its long-term minimum and maximum, so that the data is normalized by the historical range of NDVI values for the same time period.

span.label: the e-Delphi procedure: round one identifies candidate impacts, round two ranks them, and the top six become the review's scope
span.quote: The impact categories that are the focus of this research were initially identified with expert consultation using a qualitative two-round e-Delphi method \ [11, 12\] with 13 participants. The first round was used to identify potential impacts of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on food supply chains based on the hypothesis that significant impacts on the effectiveness and responsiveness of global food supply chains are the result of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. The second round asked participants to rank the impacts identified in the first round. The top six impacts defined the impact areas followed up in the review synthesis.

span.label: wheat prices rose over 40% since the war began, to levels last seen in the 2007-08 World Food Price Crisis
span.quote: Since the war began, wheat prices have risen over forty percent, to prices not seen since the 2007–2008 World Food Price Crisis

span.label: FAO estimates 20-30% of the area allocated to winter cereal, maize and sunflower seed will not be harvested or planted
span.quote: estimates that 20–30% of the areas allocated to winter cereal, maize, and sunflower seed production will not be harvested or planted this spring.

span.label: 49% of winter wheat and 38% of rye due for harvest in July-August 2022 sat in occupied or war-affected areas
span.quote: Logistics and location stifle supply with the UN FAO estimating that 49 percent of winter wheat and 38 percent of rye to be harvested in July–August 2022 are in occupied or war-affected areas

span.label: only 20% of 1,300 large agri-businesses surveyed had enough fuel to plant; about 70% of Ukraine's petrol and diesel came from Russia and Belarus
span.quote: FAO reports that only 20% of 1300 large agri-businesses surveyed by the Ukrainian Government have enough fuel for planting this spring

span.label: Ukraine produces 29.1% of global sunflower oil and exports 44% of global supply; it is the largest exporter of sunflower seeds
span.quote: Ukraine produces 29.1% of the global sunflower oil, and exports 44% of the global supply of sunflower oil. Ukraine is the largest exporter of sunflower seeds globally.

span.label: dependency figures: Egypt and Libya take two-thirds of their wheat from these two countries, Lebanon 80%, and Russia takes 73% of its barley imports from Ukraine
span.quote: For instance, India, China, and some Middle East countries rely on imports of sunflower oil from Russia and Ukraine, while Egypt and Libya obtain two-thirds of their wheat supply from these countries \ [19\]. Lebanon is supplied with 80% of its wheat from Ukraine \ [18\]. Ethiopia and Yemen are vulnerable countries that heavily rely on wheat imports from Ukraine and Russia \ [22\]. Lithuania, China, and India obtain more than 80% of their maize imports from Ukraine. Interestingly, Russia obtains 73% of its barley imports from Ukraine

span.label: central Oblasts showed a 20-25% reduction in Vegetation Condition Index against March 2021
span.quote: The central Oblasts are where Ukraine’s major agricultural crops are produced and it can be seen that these central regions have a 20–25% reduction in VCI currently suggesting growth and planting is significantly reduced.

span.label: THE PAPER'S OWN FIGURES DISAGREE: Ukraine is the SECOND largest cereal exporter in section 3.2.1 and the FOURTH largest in section 3.2.4, each with its own citation
span.quote: Ukraine exported more than $9.4bn worth of cereals in 2020, around one-fifth of its total exports, and it is ranked second global cereal exporter, whereas the US is first ranked

span.label: and the smaller version of the same: wheat production 3.2% of global in one section, 3.3% in another; exports 9.1% and then 9%
span.quote: Wheat is typically highlighted by current commenters. Ukraine’s wheat production is 3.3% of the total global wheat production

span.label: for each person killed directly in the war, nine may be killed indirectly, with child and birth-related mortality significantly affected
span.quote: For each person killed directly in the war, nine may be killed indirectly; with child and birth-related mortality significantly affected and infectious diseases at risk of re-emerging

span.label: recovery timescales differ by species: poultry within months of a maize harvest, cattle three or four years
span.quote: The expected 2022 mass slaughter of beef cattle will impact Ukrainian cattle farming for years. Cattle farming would likely not recover until three or four years after access to consistent animal feed was reestablished.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.3390/foods11142098.
